item.title: github: Pull requests: Saved whitespace preferences and improved split view
item.description:
GitHub added two review UI changes on the pull request Files changed page: whitespace visibility preferences are now saved across pull requests, and new/deleted files have improved split-view behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: vscode: Modernizing the VS Code UI
item.description:
The article says VS Code’s interface is being updated based on developer feedback, with changes focused on layout density, editor tabs, themes, and responsiveness. It points readers to the full post for details.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.98
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.98 adds Gemini 4 Argon support, improves command hook reliability, and fixes several session and UI/input issues.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: dotnet: Build Agentic UI with the new Blazor AI components
item.description:
Microsoft announced new Blazor AI components for building agentic UI in .NET. The components target streamed content, tool use, approvals, shared state, and generative experiences.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI
item.description:
GitHub Actions workflow run queries in the API and UI now return a less precise but more accurate total count for search results across filters like workflow, event, status, and branch.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page generally available
item.description:
GitHub has generally available a refreshed repository pull requests page for all users. The update is intended to make pull requests easier to find and act on from one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Designing product simplicity for the AI era
item.description:
The article asks whether shared design components are sufficient for a seamless product experience, or whether designers need to prioritize simplicity over complexity to create consistency. It frames this as a product design question for the AI era.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog
